report.notes: containment.finish() records any spawn without a job in a sticky module-level _TAINTED list that makes every later precheck() contained=False for the rest of the driver run, and adds the job to _OPEN_JOBS before terminate/empty-check so a failed TerminateJobObject or QueryInformationJobObject leaves the job for precheck() to re-check (fail closed until confirmed empty). Four new fake-kernel32 test cases (create_fails, assign_fails, terminate raising, active raising, each followed by precheck) fail on 73bdbef (checked with a git archive export because worktree creation was denied) and pass now; full tests/dev_workflow: 226 passed, 5 skipped (Windows-only, PLATFORM-GATED). Docs updated. Limit, unchanged by this repair: _TAINTED and _OPEN_JOBS live in the driver process's memory only, so a no-job process that outlives the driver process is not seen by a later driver process. Real Windows job objects not exercised here.

rounds.independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: finish() returns contained=False when job is None (create/assign failed; process resumed outside any job) or when api.terminate/_wait_empty raises, but records nothing: _OPEN_JOBS is appended only on the success path, and the leaked job handle is never closed, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE never fires. precheck() only iterates _OPEN_JOBS, so it returns contained=True. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/test_probe_r201.py using the repo's FakeApi: assign_fails -> finish {'contained': False} -> precheck {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}; terminate raising OSError -> finish {'contained': False, 'reason': 'job not verified: ...'} -> precheck {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}. run_cmd discards finish()'s result, so a gate's leftover process (taskkill /T is best effort and misses re-parented orphans) can run alongside the next reviewer, whose containment_pre is True. URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md claims every earlier job is re-checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a module-level 'tainted' record: any spawn without a job, any finish() failure (terminate/query error, n>0) must make every later precheck() return contained=False until the owner clears it (or keep the failed job in _OPEN_JOBS and close it on terminate failure). Add fake-kernel32 tests for assign_fails/create_fails/terminate-raises followed by precheck().
findings.title: Windows precheck() reports contained=True after an earlier worker/gate ran without a job or whose TerminateJobObject/empty-wait failed (R2-01 not fixed)

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/test_probe_w2.py: launcher '"%~dp0cmd.exe" /c "%~dp0real.bat" %*' gives realpath real.bat, interpreter cmd.exe, no error/unlaunchable. Any non-.exe/.com quoted file, including .bat/.cmd, counts as the 'script', and '%*' is accepted anywhere in the text (e.g. in a REM line). The reviewer then runs through cmd.exe, without /c, so stdin (the prompt) could be read as commands. This contradicts the plan's 'never through cmd.exe'. It needs a launcher already trusted at PLAN.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse a bound program whose basename is cmd.exe/powershell.exe/pwsh.exe, and refuse scripts with .bat/.cmd/.ps1 extensions; require %* on the line that names the program.
findings.title: A .cmd launcher naming cmd.exe and a .bat is bound and launched as [cmd.exe, x.bat]

findings.evidence: _run catches OSError from proc.communicate() (after containment.spawn succeeded and the process was resumed) and returns status FAILED without containment.finish(proc). On Windows the job is neither terminated, nor appended to _OPEN_JOBS, nor recorded in _TAINTED, and the handle stays open, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE does not fire. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe/test_probe_unfinished.py with the repo's FakeApi/FakeProc: communicate raises OSError(23): job 1 = {'active': 1, 'terminated': False}, _OPEN_JOBS=[], _TAINTED=[], next C.precheck() = {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}. On Linux the leftover worker is a direct child in another session and the next sweep_orphans kills it, so only Windows is affected. Low likelihood: CPython swallows BrokenPipeError/EINVAL on the stdin write.
findings.suggested_fix: Register each job in _OPEN_JOBS at spawn time (remove it only once precheck/finish verified it empty), or call containment.finish(proc) in a finally on every path after a successful spawn (also run_cmd on non-TimeoutExpired exceptions).
findings.title: Windows: a worker whose communicate() raises OSError after spawn is never finished; its job stays unterminated and untracked, and the next precheck() reports contained=True
